title: Photosynthesis
seo_title: Grade 7 Photosynthesis Worksheets: Inputs, Outputs, Chloroplasts and Experiments
standard_text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on photosynthesis (NGSS MS-LS1-6): carbon dioxide, water and light in, sugar and oxygen out, chloroplasts, and evidence from plant experiments. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Plants make sugar from CO₂, water and light.
key_sub: Photosynthesis brings matter (carbon) and energy (from sunlight) into living things and releases oxygen.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis is how plants, algae and some bacteria make their own food in chloroplasts:

carbon dioxide + water + light energy → glucose (sugar) + oxygen
6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2

Matter: carbon atoms from CO2 in the air become part of sugar, which builds the plant's body. Energy: light energy is stored in the sugar. Animals that eat plants get that matter and energy. Plants do not get their food from the soil; roots take in water and minerals.

Example

Where does a tree get most of its mass?

Carbon comes from CO₂ in the air.

Answer: carbon dioxide from the air

Example

What gas bubbles from a water plant in bright light?

Oxygen is an output.

Answer: oxygen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking a tree's mass comes mostly from the soil.
  • Mixing up the inputs (CO₂, water, light) and the outputs (sugar, oxygen).

faq.q: What are the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis?
faq.a: Inputs: carbon dioxide, water and light energy. Outputs: glucose (sugar) and oxygen.

faq.q: Where does a plant's mass come from?
faq.a: Mostly from carbon dioxide in the air, which photosynthesis turns into sugar and then into plant material.
It makes the food at the base of food webs and the oxygen that animals breathe.

items.q: Where in a plant cell does photosynthesis happen?
items.e: Chloroplasts contain green chlorophyll.

items.q: Jack lists the parts of photosynthesis. Is light energy an input or an output?
items.e: Light energy comes from the sun and is captured by chlorophyll.

items.q: How does energy from the sun end up in an animal that eats a plant?
c: The sun heats the animal's food.
Animals absorb sunlight through their skin.
Light energy is stored in sugar made by the plant; the animal eats the plant.
items.e: Photosynthesis brings energy into food webs.

items.q: Zoe asks where water fits in photosynthesis. Which is true?
c: It stores energy and is used as food and building material.
It comes from the sun and is captured by chlorophyll.
It comes from the soil through the roots.
It is released into the air through the leaves.
items.e: Water comes from the soil through the roots.

items.q: Why is photosynthesis important for animals and people?
c: It is not important for animals.
It makes the oxygen we breathe and the food at the base of food webs.
items.e: Life depends on it.

items.q: What does photosynthesis make?
items.e: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

items.q: Luis lists the parts of photosynthesis. Is water an input or an output?
items.e: Water comes from the soil through the roots.

items.q: What happens to the sugar a plant makes?
c: The plant uses it for energy and to build new cells, and stores some as starch.
items.e: Sugar is both fuel and building material.
